item.title: CineSense 2.129.1
item.description:
CineSense 2.129.1

  • Opening CineSense from Downloads no longer adds a login item for a copy macOS deletes on restart. It starts at login once it is in your Applications folder — and if you choose "Not Now" on the move offer, it now says so.
  • Click the CineSense icon in the menu bar for its menu; right-click it for the ingest panel (it was the other way round). The panel still appears by itself when a card goes in, and stays in the menu as Ingest Panel.
  • CloudSense's panel: two clear icons switch between the big card and the compact list, a bigger gear opens its settings, and "Stay awake" (a moon and a switch) sits alone at the bottom. Clicking the upload line in the menu always opens the big card.
  • A single large video uploads over one connection to a Storage Box or SFTP server, so a day of one big file goes slower than a day of many. The panel now says so when it happens, and Test connection shows that one-connection speed and what a single 100 GB file would take.
  • Copy Diagnostics reports memory the way About This Mac does (a 64 GB Mac says 64 GB).

item.title: CineSense 2.129.0
item.description:
CineSense 2.129.0

  • CineSense is now signed by Bryzr Studio and notarised by Apple: open it and macOS asks only the usual "downloaded from the internet — Open?". No Terminal commands, no System Settings detour.
  • Opened from Downloads, CineSense offers to move itself into Applications, where it starts at login and updates install.
  • Updates come by themselves: CineSense checks once a day, and a new version is a line at the top of its menu — nothing pops up. An update never installs while a card, a transfer or an upload is in progress; it waits, then CineSense relaunches by itself. Settings → About → Check for Updates checks now, and "Receive beta updates" offers test versions first.
  • Something went wrong? Menu → Copy Diagnostics shows exactly what it will gather, can hide your card and folder names, and puts it all in a folder in Downloads for you to email to beta@bryzrstudio.com. CineSense never sends anything itself, and never includes footage, passwords or keys.
